title: Jaren model document
description: A jaren-model document declares the collections of a store: each collection is a JSON Schema for its documents, a key declaration (an RFC 6901 pointer for caller-supplied keys, or null with a declared identity for store-allocated ones), and the indexes over singular JSONPath expressions. A model declares collections (the storage subset: every property JSONB, no relations), entities (the relational subset: keys, typed columns, relations via the x-entity vocabulary), or both; vocabulary is added to THIS format, never as a second format.

collections.description: Collection name (an identifier) to collection declaration.

entities.description: Entity name (an identifier) to entity declaration. The x-entity vocabulary lives INSIDE each entity schema's property subschemas and is documented in MODEL-FORMAT.md §9; stripping it leaves a plain JSON Schema.

collection.description: One collection: a document schema, the key declaration, and the declared indexes. A collection without a key pointer MUST declare how keys are allocated; allocation is declared, never guessed.

schema.description: The JSON Schema every stored document validates against (through the injected hook). Also the type source for indexed paths.

key.description: Where the caller-supplied key lives in the document, as an RFC 6901 pointer selecting at least one member — or null when the store allocates.

identity.description: How keys come to be: 'caller' (the default when a key pointer is declared), or — only with "key": null — 'uuid' (crypto.randomUUID) or 'integer' (database-allocated).

indexes.description: Declared indexes; each singular path becomes a generated column plus an index.

intervals.description: Declared intervals: each names a member the schema types as an object whose start and end are both required integers, each bound indexed by its path. Every stored span is then half-open (start < end) for every writer, enforced by the store before the statement and by a CHECK on the table, and $overlaps over it plans exactly.

x-rename.description: Migration hint: this collection was previously named the given identifier. Read by the migration planner (a rename cannot be inferred from a diff); ignored by the store.

interval.description: One declared interval over a span member: a name, unique within its collection, that names the table's CHECK constraint <name>_interval; the singular path of the span member; and, optionally, the longest span the collection holds.

name.description: The interval name, unique within its collection; <name>_interval, the constraint it names, fits 63 bytes.

path.description: A singular JSONPath expression selecting the span member — an object the schema types with required integer start and end bounds, each indexed by its own path.

maxDuration.description: The longest span the collection holds, in milliseconds: end - start <= maxDuration, held by the store before the statement and by the table's CHECK for every other writer.

index.description: One index over a singular JSONPath expression (or a composite over several). A non-singular path is rejected at open (JD0004). A derived index computes indexable scalars from the selected member instead of indexing it directly. An index may instead declare an expression: a closed computation over members, scalars and host-declared deterministic functions.

name.description: The index name, unique within its collection.

path.description: A singular JSONPath expression into the stored document ($.email), or a non-empty array of them for a composite index.

expression.description: Index a computed value rather than a member: a closed expression over declared members, JSON scalars and functions the host declared deterministic. Mutually exclusive with path and derive (JD0004) — an expression names the members it reads itself.

unique.description: Whether the index enforces uniqueness. Defaults to false.

where.description: A partial index: a bounded condition in the query grammar, and the index holds only the rows it is true for, so a unique index refuses a second row only where both satisfy it. Operands are top-level members ($.<member>) the index may read and scalar literals: $eq, $ne, $lt, $le, $gt, $ge, $eq against a $seq list of literals, $exists, $and, $or, $not. A null literal, a $seq item of a type the member does not hold, arithmetic, any other member, a condition nested deeper than 64 levels and one that lowers to a constant as written are refused at open (JD0004). A collection condition reads members the collection already indexes by their path, each of one scalar type that excludes null (a JSON null and a missing member are one SQL NULL in a generated column); a derived index takes none. It assumes conforming documents: without a validation hook a null or mistyped member reads as a missing one.

derive.description: Derive columns from the selected member instead of indexing it: 'geohash' (one TEXT cell column, precision required), 'bbox' (four REAL columns — west, south, east, north), or 'vector' (one packed BLOB column holding the l2-normalized Float32 form of an array of numbers, dims required; stored on every driver, with no B-tree over it — a fetch-and-rank plan reads it whole). A derived index is never unique.

precision.description: Geohash cell length in characters, 1-12. Required beside derive: 'geohash' and refused anywhere else — there is no safe default, because the right cell size depends on the query radius, which the model cannot know.

dims.description: The width of a derive: 'vector' column in components, 1-8192. Required beside derive: 'vector' and refused anywhere else: the width is the column's identity — two widths over one path are two columns — and a member that is not an array of exactly this many finite numbers stores NULL in the column (the document itself still stores). Constrain the member with minItems/maxItems equal to dims in the collection's schema so a wrong-width vector is refused at the write instead.

physical.description: The shape a derive: 'bbox' index takes on disk: 'columns' (the default) is four generated columns under one B-tree; 'rtree' keeps the same four columns and adds a SQLite R*Tree virtual table beside the collection, kept in sync by declared triggers, with no B-tree over the columns. The logical meaning of derive: 'bbox' is identical either way. Refused on any other index kind, and on a driver without the module it falls back to 'columns' and says so through explain().prefilters[].via.

entity.description: One entity: an object schema whose top-level properties map to columns per the hybrid rule (scalars become typed columns, nested shapes stay JSONB); keys, one-column indexes, defaults and relations are declared with x-entity inside the schema, and composite, unique or partial indexes with indexes.

indexes.description: Entity-level indexes (MODEL-FORMAT §9.2): composite, unique or partial. The x-entity unique and index flags stay the one-column shorthand.

x-rename.description: Declares this entity as the rename of the named from-model entity (MIGRATION-FORMAT §9): a rename is declared, never inferred.

type.description: SQLite affinity, or an exact catalog type in a schema-qualified native layout.

defaultValue.description: A literal SQLite value or closed structural $sql expression; planTable validates its operator and contextual semantics.

check.description: A literal SQLite value or closed structural $sql expression; planTable validates its operator and contextual semantics.

generatedExpression.description: A literal SQLite value or closed structural $sql expression; planTable validates its operator and contextual semantics.

constraints.description: Structural SQLite declarations validated by planTable.

indexes.description: Structural SQLite declarations validated by planTable.

triggers.description: Structural SQLite declarations validated by planTable.

schema.description: Native schema identity, which must equal the driver-owned schema.

when.description: What an update rule judges: 'changed' (the default), an update that changes a counted column, or 'assigned', every update that assigns one. Only on a rule whose on includes update.

columns.description: The members whose assignment fires an update rule: writable columns of a physical layout. Only on a rule whose on includes update, never beside when: 'changed' or effects.

effects.description: Database effects of a rule whose on includes update: each increments one non-key, non-null integer column of the row.

entityIndex.description: One entity-level index over column-mapped top-level members: a mapped scalar, a foreign key's via column or an epoch column. Composite in declared order, unique or not, partial with a where. Its physical name is <Entity>_<name>, and every name a model plans shares one namespace compared with ASCII case folded (a collision is JD0004). A document member, a nested path, derive, precision, dims, physical and an expression are refused (JD0004): an entity table has no generated column.

name.description: The index name, unique within its entity.

path.description: A top-level member ($.employeeId), or a non-empty array of them for a composite index.

unique.description: Whether the index enforces uniqueness. Defaults to false.

where.description: A partial index: a bounded condition in the query grammar, and the index holds only the rows it is true for, so a unique index refuses a second row only where both satisfy it. Operands are top-level members ($.<member>) the index may read and scalar literals: $eq, $ne, $lt, $le, $gt, $ge, $eq against a $seq list of literals, $exists, $and, $or, $not. A null literal, a $seq item of a type the member does not hold, arithmetic, any other member, a condition nested deeper than 64 levels and one that lowers to a constant as written are refused at open (JD0004). An entity condition reads column-mapped members other than epoch columns; a member absent from a row is never equal, unequal or ordered.

expression.description: One node of an index expression: a member path, a JSON scalar, or a call to a function the host declared. Exactly one of the three, and nothing else — an index expression is never SQL text, and the function it names is resolved for arity and determinism at open (JD0004).

member.description: A singular JSONPath expression into the stored document ($.email).

value.description: A JSON scalar. A null or a compound has no place in an index expression.

call.description: The name of a function the host declared through openStore({ expressions }). The store refuses a name it was not given, a wrong arity, and one not declared deterministic — before any DDL.

args.description: The arguments, in order. Order is significant: sub(a, b) and sub(b, a) are different expressions and different columns.
